noise_6step_check.note: §B computed on the peeled residual after stripping the best deterministic fit (brightness_darken_gamma_RGB:3), pair 0. Residual std 31.6.
noise_6step_check.diagnosis: §B says IMPULSE by extreme_pct and YCrCb by rgb_ratio, but both are artifacts of the unmodelled chroma gain: extreme_pct is inflated by structured global mismatch (spatial_corr=0.96), impulse is independently ruled out because pair-0 target has ~0% channel values at 255 (impulse salt always writes exactly 255, surviving any later darkening) while its 4.04% clipped values are all dark-side. Dense gaussian noise (RGB/YCrCb/speckle/poisson) is ruled out by the wavelet MAD: target residual sigma is 0.74-1.24 on all 5 pairs while every dense-noise simulation yields 9.9-15.6. Conclusion: chroma texture comes from deterministic chroma-space amplification of the clean image's own micro-texture (saturate_strengthen), not an additive noise function.

support_validation.conclusion: 0/4 support pairs reached MATCH/PARTIAL for the noise-bearing candidate. The recurring, physically specific failures (target residual sigma 0.74-1.24 vs sim 9.9-12.2 everywhere; ccc 0.79 on pair3; mean-shift over-darkening on 3/5 pairs) indicate the additive-noise step is spurious and that gamma severity is biased high on darker content. The deterministic gamma + saturation composite is therefore promoted to the primary prediction (severity inferred, not directly simulated due to the 25-test hard budget), with the noise-bearing candidate retained as alternative #1.

final_decision.rationale: Deterministic core: gamma-style darkening (content-dependent mean shift, shadow clipping up to 30% on the dark star-trail pair, highlights preserved) plus a YCrCb-space chroma gain (channel-correlated residual ccc up to 0.79, vivid neon colours, chroma ratio 1.27-3.74 and 255-free clipping). Compression, blur, quantization and additive noise are all contradicted by measurements (block_boundary ~1.001, slope flat, unique_G 232, residual wavelet sigma 0.74-1.24 on 5/5 pairs vs 9.9-15.6 for any noise simulation). Open knobs: saturation severity (YCrCb x3 gives chroma 1.6-1.9, target up to 3.74 -> sev4 x8 estimated, +/-1) and gamma severity (sev3 fits pair0 exactly but over-darkens pairs 2-4 by 6-13 levels; sev2 would undershoot pair0).

reanalysis.overlooked_signal_1_nonpointwise: R0's gamma+saturation family is pointwise. clean pair1 contains 12078 identical (255,255,255) pixels; under any pointwise map they must share one output, but the target maps them to a wide distribution: 10/25/50/75/90th pct = 165/194/218/232/236, std 32, per-channel means R=213.0 G=207.6 B=203.6. A spatially varying (neighbourhood or random) operation is therefore mandatory. R0 never tested this.
reanalysis.overlooked_signal_2_highlight_destructio: All five targets contain EXACTLY zero channel values at 255 (and zero at 254), while clean pair1 has 1.778% exact 255 and pair3 1.474%. Gamma (255^g=255), HSV saturation (V preserved) and any LUT with 255->255 cannot be the final chain; pointwise subtractive shifts are excluded too because target maxima 226-246 exceed 255-25.5. Only a spatial mix (blur of clipped noise) before a V-preserving saturation explains this.
reanalysis.overlooked_signal_3_variance_collapse: pair3 (dark star-trail content) target variance_ratio 0.362; pointwise saturate_strengthen_HSV:2 alone yields 0.794, blur_gaussian:3 alone 0.18 gm/masked, blur+saturation yields 0.351-0.362. R0's blur rejection came from gm_ratio/spectral_slope, which the SKILL marks unreliable in mixed (high-saturation clipping) degradation.
reanalysis.overlooked_signal_4_chroma_seed: pair0 clean chroma std 9.06 -> target 33.84 (x3.73); satHV2 alone reaches only x1.94. The missing chroma variation is a pre-blur noise field: gaussian_RGB sev4 (sigma=0.2*255=51) then blur_gaussian sev3 leaves wavelet sigma at 0.1-0.25 (the estimator R0 used measures HIGH-frequency noise, which the blur removes), but after S x6 the blurred field becomes the target's dense chroma speckle (x3.71-3.73 on pair0).
reanalysis.threshold_boundary: R0 exhausted its 25-test budget without ever simulating its final composite. Direct support simulation of the R0 pipeline now gives PSNR 15.22/14.80/16.44/14.00/15.87 dB and produces ~28% channel values at 255 (target: 0%), so the R0 composite is worse than several intermediates it had rejected.
reanalysis.physical_order: noise(priority 0) -> blur(priority 1) -> saturation(priority 2) is exactly the order enforced by the challenge generator; no compression and no brightness step are needed to explain any signal.

All stable statistics coincide: extreme_pct 55.9/55.9, 66.6/66.6, 63.0/62.9, 66.8/66.6, 65.1/65.2; zero_ratio identical to 4 decimals; spatial_corr 0.9504/0.9504, 0.9519/0.9514, 0.9375/0.9368, 0.8393/0.8388, 0.9425/0.9417; rgb_ratio 2.73/2.73, 2.79/2.75, 1.65/1.62, 1.29/1.27, 1.44/1.43; cross_ch_corr 0.473/0.474, 0.207/0.203, 0.165/0.163, 0.225/0.219, 0.204/0.203; ch_stds and residual_std (30.9/30.8, 20.6/20.5, 22.1/22.0, 15.4/15.4, 20.5/20.4) also coincide. vm_slope and var_slope flip sign between the two residuals (and across seed controls), confirming they are not reliable estimators on this residual. residual_exhaustion_evidence.variance_budget: Var(target - mean of 5 seeded sims) / Var(single seed field) = 1.21, 1.194, 1.191, 1.216, 1.213 on pairs 0-4; theory for a statistically exact pipeline is 1 + 1/5 = 1.20. Zero excess deterministic variance remains.
residual_exhaustion_evidence.fwhm: residual autocorrelation FWHM of target-vs-sim equals the sim-vs-sim seed control on all 5 pairs (8/8, 8/8, 8/8, 4/4, 8/8 px); the only verify_signals mismatch is therefore intrinsic to independent noise seeds when noise precedes a blur.
residual_exhaustion_evidence.conditioned_bias: mean residual per 25-level clean-brightness bin |<=0.5| levels (one pair4 top bin +1.4), per edge-magnitude bin <=0.45, per chroma-magnitude bin <=0.5 on a ~180 scale -> no leftover tonal/blur/saturation-curve mismatch.
residual_exhaustion_evidence.conditioned_variance: residual-variance ratio target:seed-control is flat 2.0-2.2 across brightness bins and chroma bins -> additive homoscedastic noise; excludes Poisson (var~mean) and speckle (var~mean^2).
